world_workbench_description: Software someone can still understand tomorrow.
home_lead: I build web applications and enjoy making complex things a little easier to understand. This is my small place on the internet — somewhere between work, hobbies, and a fairly large enthusiasm for science fiction.
home_quote: “Usually somewhere between code, architecture questions, and: could we make this simpler?”
home_section_one_body: I like clear thinking, small feedback loops, and software that respects the people using it. The useful solution usually starts by understanding the real constraint.
home_section_two_body: Orbit is a quiet map of my work, current interests, and side quests. Every destination remains a real page, even without the visual system around it.
current_title: What has my attention right now.
current_lead: No roadmap and no artificially filled feed. Just a small snapshot of the things currently on my desk or in my head.
current_detail_two_value: Finding a sci-fi game without an 80-hour backlog
current_detail_three_value: Go outside more. Keep fewer tabs.
current_quote: “Maybe this will become a blog one day. Today it is simply my homepage.”
current_section_one_body: I am exploring dependable AI-assisted product workflows, from shaping a useful problem to shipping software that can be understood and maintained.
current_section_two_body: The recurring theme is leverage without losing judgment: better tools, tighter feedback, and deliberate decisions about where automation should stop.
workbench_title: Software someone can still understand tomorrow.
workbench_lead: I care not only whether something works, but whether other people can understand, change, and continue developing it.
workbench_detail_one_value: Maintainable web applications and understandable APIs
workbench_detail_two_value: Share context instead of hiding decisions
workbench_detail_three_value: Only as much magic as is genuinely helpful
workbench_quote: “Pragmatism is not indifference. And good tickets are part of developer experience too.”
workbench_section_one_body: Start with the user journey, make state explicit, and keep the architecture proportional to the problem. Accessibility and performance are part of the design, not a final pass.
workbench_section_two_body: TypeScript and modern web platforms are frequent companions, but the stack follows the job. I value strong types, observable behavior, automated checks, and small deployable changes.
workbench_projects_body: Veo explores AI-assisted video workflows, kijk is a product-focused software project, and Orbit is the website you are navigating now. Their source and progress are public on GitHub.
side_quests_lead: I like things where progress is visible: finding a path, building something, and understanding a little better how everything fits together.
side_quests_detail_two_value: Hiking and trading the screen for a wider view
side_quests_detail_three_value: LEGO, small pieces, and big systems
side_quests_quote: “Unfortunately, my preferred fast travel usually only works in games.”
side_quests_section_one_body: Hiking and training provide a useful change of scale: steady progress, real terrain, and fewer notifications.
side_quests_section_two_body: Games, LEGO, and small creative projects are laboratories for systems thinking, storytelling, and the pleasure of making something just because it is fun.
comms_lead: If you want to talk about software, LEGO, science fiction, or a good hiking trail, the communications channel is open.
comms_detail_three_value: Friendly, direct, and without a sales sequence
comms_quote: “No tracking beacons. No newsletter popup. Just a regular email.”
comms_section_one_body: The most direct channel is email. You can also find my public work on GitHub or connect with me on LinkedIn.
comms_section_two_body: A short note about what you are building, what is difficult, and why it matters is always a helpful way to begin.
